transcript.content: Hello, welcome in. What brings you to see me today?

Well, I'm here because... well, for over a year now, I’ve been trying to get someone, anyone really, to take seriously what's happening at work. The new ticket rotation and these constant security audits, they are being used to build a paper trail against me. I know it. Management keeps showing me these logs and saying it’s just policy, but I know what I see. 

It reminds me of this time back in '98, I was working on a server migration for this small logistics firm. They had this old Novell NetWare setup, and the cabling... you wouldn't believe the cabling. It looked like a plate of spaghetti dropped behind the racks. I spent three whole weekends just tracing wires. My wife at the time, she hated it. She'd say, "You love those cables more than me." We got divorced a few years later. Not because of the cables, obviously, but she did take the dog. A golden retriever named Buster. Great dog. 

Anyway, what was I saying? Oh, right, the audits. Yeah, they say it's policy, but I've been a computer support specialist for a long time, and I know when a system is being rigged.
Have you ever heard voices or sounds that other people couldn't hear?

Voices? No, no. I don't hear people talking when nobody's around, if that's what you're getting at. My hearing is mostly just shot from the server rooms, honestly. 

Though, you know, when you do this job long enough, you do get an ear for certain pitches. Like a failing hard drive. The old mechanical ones, they'd make this specific sound. Back in... oh, it must have been 2008, we had this huge batch of Seagate drives. The 1.5 terabyte models. They had a terrible firmware bug, just awful. I could walk into the datacenter and hear this faint clicking over the fans, and I'd tell my manager, "Greg, drive three in the array is about to brick." 

He never listened to me, of course. Greg drove this pristine 1990 Mazda Miata. Cherry red. He spent more time talking about the imported wax he used on that car than he did looking at the network topology. Used to keep a special microfiber cloth right on his desk, wouldn't let anyone touch it. He actually tried to expense the car wax once, said he used it on the server racks. Accounting had a field day with that one. 

But, uh... wait, what was I answering? Oh, voices. Right. No, no voices. Just normal sounds.

Outside of my job? Oh, you mean like... no, no. Everything else is completely normal. Outside of this whole mess with the ticket rotation and the audits, I do fine. I keep the house in order, pay the bills, help my wife out. 

Actually, I was just helping her set up this new smart sprinkler system she wanted for the backyard. She loves her hydrangeas. But the app for this thing... it requires a 2.4 gigahertz Wi-Fi band, which is standard for cheap IoT devices, but our home router was auto-steering everything to 5 gigahertz. I had to go into the admin settings and split the bands. Took me all Sunday afternoon because the manufacturer's interface was a joke. It actually reminded me of this old Linksys router I had back in 2003, the WRT54G. Blue and black case, dual antennas. Legendary piece of hardware. You could flash custom open-source firmware on it—Tomato, DD-WRT, all of that. I used to run a custom script on mine just to prioritize network traffic for my online chess games. I was pretty highly ranked on Yahoo Chess back then. I actually played a guy once who claimed he was a grandmaster from Russia, but I'm pretty sure he was just using a chess engine because his response times were exactly three seconds per move, every single time. 

Anyway... sorry, what was I saying? Oh, right, my life outside of work. Yeah, no, I manage everything fine. Even at work, honestly, I handle all the technical parts of my job perfectly. Nobody has ever said my work is sloppy or disorganized. I know what I'm doing. It's just that specific paper trail they're building with the tickets. But everywhere else? I'm totally fine.
